properties.natural_language: External calls to contracts with hardcoded gas assumptions must not assume SLOAD costs less than 800 gas.
Transaction call data crossing from an external caller into gas-sensitive code paths must carry sufficient gas for repriced opcodes (SLOAD=800, BALANCE=700, EXTCODEHASH=700).
The ERC-165 supportsInterface callback must not use SLOAD when operating within a 30,000 gas stipend, as SLOAD now costs 800 gas.
After EIP-1884 activation, SLOAD gas cost must always be 800, BALANCE must always be 700, and EXTCODEHASH must always be 700.
After gas deduction for a repriced opcode, the remaining gas must be non-negative for execution to proceed; otherwise the transaction must revert.
After executing the SELFBALANCE opcode (0x47), the EVM stack must contain the balance of the currently executing contract and exactly 5 gas must have been consumed.
The SELFBALANCE opcode must always return the same value as BALANCE(ADDRESS) when called within the same execution context, but at 5 gas instead of 700.
Ether transfers via transfer() or send() triggering a fallback function must not depend on SLOAD being available within the 2300 gas stipend.
After looking up the gas cost in the EIP-1884 updated schedule, the returned cost must match the specified values for the given opcode.
After gas validation, execution must proceed to trie access only if gas remaining is non-negative; otherwise a gas validation failed state must be entered.
Contracts must not assume that SLOAD can be performed within a 2300 gas stipend, as this is no longer sufficient post-EIP-1884.
The gas cost increases must accurately reflect the actual computational cost of trie access operations to prevent DoS attacks.
Solidity and other compilers must not generate code that depends on specific SLOAD/BALANCE gas costs being below EIP-1884 values.
Block proposer timestamp data must be validated as within acceptable protocol bounds before being used in difficulty calculation.
Parent block difficulty value must be authenticated via consensus before being used in child difficulty calculation.
Uncle references in parent block header must be cryptographically verified via unclesHash before determining the uncle factor.
After checking uncle count, the uncle factor must be set to 2 if uncles exist and 1 otherwise.
After computing the adjustment factor, its value must be bounded between -99 and the uncle_factor value.
After computing child difficulty, the result must equal parent.difficulty + (parent.difficulty // 2048) * adj_factor.
The EIP-100 difficulty adjustment must account for uncle rate such that manipulating uncle rate does not increase effective issuance.
Uncle rate gaming attempts from malicious miners must be neutralized by the EIP-100 formula before affecting difficulty.
After timestamp validation, the block timestamp must be acceptable for difficulty calculation before setting the difficulty field.
After setting the difficulty field in the block header, the value must be the computed child difficulty.
The uncle factor derivation from len(parent.uncles) must use only block header data (unclesHash), not full uncle block data.
The target average block time including uncles must remain approximately 15 seconds under normal network conditions.
Transaction hash announcements from peer nodes must be treated as untrusted; actual transaction data must be fetched and independently validated.
All blob data received from peers via PooledBlobs must have hash correspondence validated against requested vhashes before acceptance.
Blob versioned hashes must be extracted from the transaction before requesting blob data via GetPooledBlobs.
After blob hash validation completes, only blobs whose transmitted hashes match requested vhashes must be accepted.
A node must not forward a type-3 transaction to peers until all blobs have been received and validated.
After checking blob completeness, if any blobs are missing, the transaction must be blocked from forwarding.
After building a PooledBlobs response, blobs must be in matching order to the requested vhashes, with unavailable blobs skipped.
Peers must eventually provide blob data for announced transactions; otherwise the transaction state is incomplete and mempool pollution occurs.
The separation of blob and transaction propagation must not create race conditions where a transaction is processed before its blobs arrive.
RBF scenarios must maintain blob availability when only fees change; original transaction blobs must not be discarded before replacement validation.
Attackers must not be able to efficiently enumerate blob vhashes without having observed corresponding transactions.
Standard blob security considerations must apply even though the EIP security considerations section is empty.
Error conditions for blob requests must follow standard devp2p error handling; missing blobs must be handled gracefully.
Input data to the MODEXP precompile at address 0x05 must be treated as arbitrary and untrusted, with zero-padding applied for short input.
Length fields for BASE, EXPONENT, and MODULUS must be correctly parsed as 32-byte big-endian values without integer overflow.
When input data is shorter than declared lengths, missing bytes must be treated as zero (infinite right-padding semantics).
After extracting operands, BASE, EXPONENT, and MODULUS must all be available for computation using the declared lengths.
After computing the MODEXP result, the output byte array must have length equal to the declared MODULUS length.
After gas computation, the gas cost must equal floor(mult_complexity * max(adjusted_exp_len, 1) / GQUADDIVISOR).
After checking gas availability, an out-of-gas exception must be raised if available gas is less than computed cost.
When MODULUS is zero, the result must be a zero byte array of length equal to the declared modulus length.
Excess input data beyond what the declared lengths specify must be ignored and must not affect the computation result.
The underlying big integer arithmetic must correctly handle arbitrary precision without overflow or truncation errors.
The Karatsuba multiplication approximation in gas pricing must not significantly underestimate actual computation time for any valid input.
When all three length fields are zero, the operation must return an empty byte array with minimal gas cost.
When the first 32 bytes of the exponent are all zeros, the highest bit index must be treated as 0 and adjusted_exponent_length as zero.
Receipt data received from peers in partial or complete responses must be validated using sanity checks on count, individual size, and total size before acceptance.
GetReceipts request parameters from peers must be validated: block hashes must be known, index values must be bounds-checked, and rate limiting must be applied.
Implementations must bound buffer sizes and apply recommended sanity checks to prevent memory exhaustion attacks from paginated receipt responses.
After validating receipt count, the total receipts must match the transaction count in the corresponding blocks.
After validating individual receipt sizes, each receipt size must be bounded by the transaction gas limit divided by 8.
After receipt validation failure, the misbehaving peer must be penalized by reducing their peer score or disconnecting.
After computing the next pagination index, the follow-up request must include the correct firstBlockReceiptIndex.
After checking response message size, if all receipts fit, lastBlockIncomplete must be set to 0; if they exceed the limit, lastBlockIncomplete must be set to 1.
Peers must eventually provide complete receipt data through multiple paginated requests; implementations need request timeouts and peer rotation.
An attacker must not be able to forge receipt data that passes sanity checks but represents invalid state.
DApp client authentication requests must include a nonce that is verified for freshness to prevent replay attacks.
Path permissions requested in did_authenticate must be explicitly approved by the user before granting access.
Authentication must fail with an appropriate error code if the nonce is invalid or replayed.
After user grants permissions, the wallet must create a JWS with protected header containing kid and keyFragment.
After JWS creation, the payload must be signed using secp256k1 or ed25519 and returned in general serialization format.
After decrypting a JWE, if payload paths match authenticated prefixes, cleartext must be auto-returned without user confirmation.
After decrypting a JWE, if payload paths do not match authenticated prefixes, user confirmation must be required before returning cleartext.
Wallet implementations must correctly enforce path-based permission system and must not auto-approve decryption for unauthorized paths.
Attackers must not be able to forge DID authentication responses or JWS signatures without access to the private key.
Paths must be treated as URI-like prefixes with matching done by string prefix comparison.
Nonces must be generated with sufficient randomness and uniqueness to prevent replay attacks.
DApp request arguments must be validated for proper structure including required method field before routing to wallet.
All input from potentially malicious DApps must be sanitized and rate-limited before processing.
Rate limiting must be enforced on provider requests; requests exceeding limits must be rejected.
After request validation fails, the promise must reject with an appropriate ProviderRpcError.
After wallet processes the request, the promise must resolve with the RPC result or reject with a ProviderRpcError.
After a connect event, the chainId must be emitted in hex format to all registered event listeners.
After losing all chain connections, a disconnect event must be emitted with a ProviderRpcError.
After a chain switch, a chainChanged event must be emitted with the new chainId in hex format.
After user authorizes accounts, an accountsChanged event must be emitted with the updated accounts array.
After user revokes accounts, the accounts must no longer be exposed and an accountsChanged event with an empty array must be emitted.
After determining the error code, the ProviderRpcError must be constructed with the correct code (4001, 4100, 4200, 4900, or 4901), message, and optional data.
The Provider must never contain private user data; Provider and Wallet programs must remain isolated from each other.
The browser must provide adequate isolation between DApp JavaScript and Provider internals.
Attackers must not be able to modify the Provider object after it is exposed at window.ethereum.
Filter options from JSON-RPC clients must be validated: blockHash must be mutually exclusive with fromBlock/toBlock parameters.
The blockHash parameter must be a valid 32-byte hex string before block lookup.
After block lookup failure, an error response with code -32000, message 'Block not found.', and the requested block hash in the data field must be returned.
After finding the block, logs must be filtered by address and topics and returned in JSON-RPC response format.
After detecting a blockHash with fromBlock/toBlock conflict, the request must be rejected with a validation error.
The blockHash must reference a canonical chain block; uncle blocks must return 'Block not found' error.
The block hash lookup operation must be efficient and must not cause denial of service under high query load.
EOF bytecode submitted for deployment must be treated as arbitrary and untrusted; full header and metadata validation must be performed.
The metadata_size field must be within valid range (1-65535) and the metadata section must be positioned before the data section.
After parsing the EOF header, all section types and sizes including optional metadata marker (0x05) must be correctly identified.
After position validation, the metadata section must be confirmed as correctly positioned before the data section, or the EOF container must be rejected.
After bytecode comparison during verification, source code must be confirmed as matching if recompiled bytecode (excluding metadata) equals deployed bytecode.
Metadata content must be treated as opaque bytes with no protocol-level validation; consumers must handle malformed content gracefully.
Metadata changes must not affect contract execution behavior; metadata must not be reachable by contract code.
Metadata content cannot be trusted to accurately represent compiler version and source references; false metadata could mislead verification.
Verification requests from external tools must be treated as untrusted; IPFS content may be unavailable or malicious.
Block range claims from peers via BlockRangeUpdate must be treated as untrusted and verified when requesting data; peers failing to serve claimed ranges must be penalized.
Receipt request parameters from peers must be untrusted; rate limiting and response size controls must be applied.
After peer status validation, the connection must proceed only if networkid, genesis, and forkid are compatible; incompatible peers must be disconnected.
After updating the local history range, peers must be notified via BlockRangeUpdate at most once per epoch (32 blocks).
After encoding receipts in eth/69 format, bloom filters must be omitted; the format must include only tx-type, post-state-or-status, cumulative-gas, and logs.
After decoding eth/69 receipts, bloom filters must be recomputed from logs if needed for local queries.
After peer selection for history request, if no peer covers the requested block range, the system must report that history is unavailable.
Sufficient nodes must continue serving historical data for clients that need it; otherwise network fragmentation occurs.
Peers that claim false block ranges to attract connections but fail to serve data must be detected and penalized.
The network must have migrated away from total difficulty reliance post-merge; removing TD from handshake must not break compatibility.
